phase: 26 — final disposition of the remaining 37 HEADWORD_COLOUR_MISMATCH findings (classification only)

source.derivation: all 110 P15 HCM records minus the 73 in the five corrected chapters = 37
source.crossCheck: P23 run1, P23 run2 and P24 control each measured HCM = 37 independently
source.p21FileNote: audit/qa-baseline-p21-diagnostic.json contains 38 HCM. The extra record is a1-11-negation speaking/311 "Nein" — the single non-reproducible artefact already discarded in Phase 22/23. Reported here, not silently reconciled: the authoritative post-fix set is 37.

classAVerification.method: Class A is identified by span colour == the default accent teal rgb(31,78,74); counted directly over all 37 records
classAVerification.corroboration: the P19/P20 audit found 11 canonical-role CSS collisions total; the 5 that ever affected a rendered token are fixed and the other 6 affect zero rendered tokens

colourAuthorities.span: the OCCURRENCE role. tokenRole()/roleFor() (chapter-app.js:898-919) resolve explicit token role → authoredClassRole → guessRole, and chapter.css .r-* paints it.
colourAuthorities.head: the LEXEME/ENTRY class. renderWordPop resolves normalizedRole from the entry first and uses the occurrence role only when the entry supplies nothing ("this only fills a genuine void", chapter-app.js:2038-2052); the colour is then var(--g-<role>) via ROLE_COLOR_VAR (:2022) and :2054, applied as an inline style.
colourAuthorities.supposedToDiffer: YES, by design — but the design does not make every difference correct. A difference is benign when the head REFINES the span within one family (G1) and is a defect symptom when the two contradict each other (G2/G3/G5).
colourAuthorities.whyHcmStillFiresOnByDesignCases: qa-engine.js:34 exempts the same surface carrying different roles at different OCCURRENCES from the role check; HCM compares two colours WITHIN one occurrence, so the exemption does not apply. That is a different comparison, not an inconsistent rule — the detector is reporting a real colour difference in every case.

a1-39 vocabulary idx 570 \"a\".head: rgb(90, 90, 96)  ink-secondary
a1-39 vocabulary idx 570 \"a\".finding: LEGITIMATE COLOUR MAPPING. chapter-app.js:2022 maps entry classes letter|name|conjunction to --ink-secondary, mirroring chapter.css:231 .r-conjunction. The surface is the letter "a" in a vocabulary list, so the popup is correct.
a1-39 vocabulary idx 570 \"a\".defectSide: the PROSE span, which carries adverb cyan for a letter

b1-22 listening idx 681 \"machen\".head: rgb(190, 24, 93)
b1-22 listening idx 681 \"machen\".finding: LEGITIMATE COLOUR MAPPING. rgb(190,24,93) = #BE185D = --g-brauchen, defined at chapter.css:61 and a member of CANONICAL_ROLES. It was missing only from CLAUDE.md’s abbreviated palette list, which is why P17/P18 could not place it. The chapter is b1-22-brauchen-zu-infinitiv, so the entry resolving to the brauchen construction is coherent.
b1-22 listening idx 681 \"machen\".defectSide: none proven — verb (span) and brauchen (head) are the same family
b1-22 listening idx 681 \"machen\".confidence: PROVEN (colour source), STRONGLY SUGGESTED (that no correction is needed)

remainingUncertainty: mechanism is PROVEN for 13 of 37 (11 via co-located ROLE_CONTRADICTS_BADGE, 2 via source-identified head colours) and STRONGLY SUGGESTED for the other 24 — the engine emits HCM with detail {span, head} only, so badge/role/headword are unavailable unless another finding fired on the same node
WHICH side to correct is a curriculum decision for every DATA/AUTHORING row; this phase does not decide it
the 3 UNRESOLVED rows (Obgleich ×3) show object→adjective for a concessive conjunction — neither colour is defensible and no evidence attributes either side
epistemicNote: no row is called a PRODUCTION DEFECT: in all 37 the two colour authorities behaved exactly as the source specifies. The disagreements originate in authored token roles and lexicon entry classes, or are benign taxonomic refinements. Equally, no row is called a DETECTOR FALSE POSITIVE: the detector correctly reports a genuine colour difference every time — whether that difference matters is the disposition, not the detection.
filesModified: none — no chapter data, CSS, chapter-app.js, qa-engine.js, lint, assertions or baselines touched; no existing artifact overwritten
